title: An empty Internal category row holds the Close with Retry
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new Internal category for this test, category A, whose Account Mappings row is empty.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, whose default internal category is category A.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 2, for internal customer B, closed, closed earlier, so another event of the organization can be seen flowing.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. Open Accounting > Accounting Events.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 4:

  • Work order 1's Close shows the status Held with the reason "Internal: [category A's name] row not mapped" and a Retry action.
  • Work order 2's events are posted: other events keep flowing.
  • The event is labelled "Work order closed · [number] · Internal".

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

  • S8-N2: “If a mapped account on either side of the entry is missing or inactive, or the posting date falls in a closed fiscal period or in none, the event gets a status Held (new in the hub) on the Accounting Events page with the reason ("No Charge: [Category] row not mapped" or "Internal: [Category] row not mapped", the list name telling the two apart (S8-R7), "Shop supplies expense is not mapped", "Inventory asset is not mapped", "Parts cost of goods sold is not mapped", "Period [name] is closed", or the hub's existing "No open fiscal period covers [date]."), the existing Retry action, and automatic retry when the mapping is saved or the period opened. Other events for the organization keep flowing. A held Close withdrawn by Reopen becomes Dismissed (S4-E1). Held exists for these work-order entries only (Close, reversal, no-charge line, and the move of a vendor bill or credit line to its category account, S8-R3); invoices, vendor bills, credits and payments keep today's statuses.”
  • Story 8, Error Handling: “Failures follow the Held path of S8-N2; nothing is shown to the advisor at Close beyond S3-N4.”
  • Key Decisions: “Close always succeeds (the one refusal is a work order that changed under the open confirmation, S3-E5). A missing account never blocks the advisor: QuickBooks posts to the ShopView Review account as it does for every other unmapped account today; AccountingHub holds the event with a Retry.”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026
